raw.title: Assumption Separation Lens
raw.family: AI-Assisted Design and KB Governance Lenses
raw.one_sentence_purpose: Diagnose whether the design artifact has a clear, testable position on assumption separation without inventing facts or relying on unsupported source claims.
phase_groups: 测试 / 验收 / 审计
when_to_use: Use during 立项与方向, 开发实现, 测试 / 验收 / 审计 when assumption separation is likely to affect player experience or production risk.
Use before accepting a design decision as stable.
Use after a prototype, playtest, design review, or project overlay produces new evidence.
what_it_reveals: Whether assumption separation is defined as an observable design concern.
Which assumptions are unsupported.
Which next experiment would produce better evidence.
diagnostic_questions: What exact artifact, player behavior, or production decision is the assumption separation lens examining?
What player experience is intended, and where is that intention visible rather than assumed?
Which rule, feedback signal, content beat, UI element, or production constraint most strongly affects assumption separation?
What evidence do we have now, and what evidence is missing before this judgment should influence scope?
What small experiment, playtest prompt, prototype change, or review task would test the riskiest assumption this week?
required_inputs: A game idea, feature spec, prototype recording, playtest note, system map, UI mockup, narrative outline, or production decision.
The intended player experience or project goal.
Known constraints, risks, and available evidence.
recommended_outputs: source-bounded AI review or evidence audit
red_flags: The review depends on assumed player reactions without evidence.
The artifact cannot show where the lens concern appears.
The proposed action changes scope without a testable reason.
common_false_positives: A polished presentation hides an untested design assumption.
A familiar genre convention is mistaken for proof that the design works.
A single player anecdote is treated as broad validation.

body_sections.heading: What It Reveals
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - Whether onboarding is defined as an observable design concern. - Which assumptions are unsupported. - Which next experiment would produce better evidence.

body_sections.heading: Diagnostic Questions
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - What exact artifact, player behavior, or production decision is the onboarding lens examining? - What player experience is intended, and where is that intention visible rather than assumed? - Which rule, feedback signal, content beat, UI element, or production constraint most strongly affects onboarding? - What evidence do we have now, and what evidence is missing before this judgment should influence scope? - What small experiment, playtest prompt, prototype change, or review task would test the riskiest assumption this week?

body_sections.heading: Required Inputs
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - A game idea, feature spec, prototype recording, playtest note, system map, UI mockup, narrative outline, or production decision. - The intended player experience or project goal. - Known constraints, risks, and available evidence.

body_sections.heading: Recommended Outputs

body_sections.heading: Red Flags
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - The review depends on assumed player reactions without evidence. - The artifact cannot show where the lens concern appears. - The proposed action changes scope without a testable reason.

body_sections.heading: Common False Positives

body_sections.heading: Purpose
body_sections.excerpt_safe: Diagnose whether the design artifact has a clear, testable position on runaway loops without inventing facts or relying on unsupported source claims.

body_sections.heading: When To Use
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - Use during 核心玩法与系统设计, 数值与经济设计, 测试 / 验收 / 审计 when runaway loops is likely to affect player experience or production risk. - Use before accepting a design decision as stable. - Use after a prototype, playtest, design review, or project overlay produces new evidence.

body_sections.heading: What It Reveals
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - Whether runaway loops is defined as an observable design concern. - Which assumptions are unsupported. - Which next experiment would produce better evidence.

body_sections.heading: Diagnostic Questions
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - What exact artifact, player behavior, or production decision is the runaway loops lens examining? - What player experience is intended, and where is that intention visible rather than assumed? - Which rule, feedback signal, content beat, UI element, or production constraint most strongly affects runaway loops? - What evidence do we have now, and what evidence is missing before this judgment should influence scope? - What small experiment, playtest prompt, prototype change, or review task would test the riskiest assumption this week?

body_sections.heading: Required Inputs
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - A game idea, feature spec, prototype recording, playtest note, system map, UI mockup, narrative outline, or production decision. - The intended player experience or project goal. - Known constraints, risks, and available evidence.

body_sections.heading: Recommended Outputs
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - system map or balance test - strengths - risks - missing evidence - suggested experiments - next design actions

body_sections.heading: Red Flags
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - The review depends on assumed player reactions without evidence. - The artifact cannot show where the lens concern appears. - The proposed action changes scope without a testable reason.

body_sections.heading: Common False Positives
body_sections.excerpt_safe: - A polished presentation hides an untested design assumption. - A familiar genre convention is mistaken for proof that the design works. - A single player anecdote is treated as broad validation.
